usageNotes: Use this to install a third-party or internally signed TLS certificate on a specific Proxmox node's web GUI (pveproxy). The caller must hold Sys.Modify on /nodes/{node}. Set restart: true to apply the certificate immediately — without it, pveproxy continues serving the old cert until manually restarted. If an ACME-managed certificate is already present, pass force: true to overwrite it; otherwise the request will fail.

examples.summary: Upload a Let's Encrypt cert bundle with private key and immediately restart pveproxy

params.certificates:
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIE...base64...==
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIE...intermediate...==
-----END CERTIFICATE-----

tips: The certificates field must be a full PEM chain — leaf cert first, followed by any intermediates — to avoid browser trust errors.
If you omit the key param, Proxmox expects the private key was previously uploaded or is embedded in the existing keystore; for a clean install always supply the key.
The response returns the parsed cert metadata (fingerprint, notafter, SANs) synchronously — there is no UPID; verify the fingerprint in the response before confirming success.
restart: true triggers a graceful pveproxy reload; active API/web sessions will reconnect automatically within a few seconds.
To revert to a self-signed cert, use the DELETE endpoint for custom certificates rather than uploading a blank value.
